blocks.title: System Overview
rows: Typical pinball playing field used to accomplish game scenario objectives displayed real-time on monitor
Portable, tabletop cabinet containing typical pinball devices controlled using modern day electronics + monitor for real-time graphics
Software defined theme packs played on generic playing field

blocks.title: Mechanical
rows: COTS materials and fasteners; 3D printed and laser cut custom parts
Hinged playfield (service access); fixed bottom shelf panel; no legs — rubber pads only

blocks.title: Electrical
rows: All solenoid firing runs through the Topedal board's Blue Pill firmware (fire pulse, then PWM hold where used); no hardware autofire (safety). The switches for DC-01 Pop bumpers, DC-02 Slingshots and DC-04 Flipper Assembly are on the same Topedal board as their coils
Digital switches connected via Topedal board's onboard direct/matrix switch inputs
Computer supporting MPF + Godot Media Controller (GMC) running Mission Pinball Framework (MPF) — game logic, scoring, game scenarios; GMC for audio/video/monitor display
USB serial between host and Topedal board(s)

blocks.title: Software
rows: Identical OPP firmware flashed to all Topedal boards (same STM32F103 processor as standard OPP), distinguished by board address; MPF config (not firmware) defines game scenario behavior
A game scenario is defined by populating a Game Scenario Framework — requires no firmware changes

Primitive — single physical switch/coil/sensor, no sub-components, assigned unique ID.
Composite — 2 or more primitives combined to perform one coordinated physical action, e.g., button + coil + EOS sensor = flipper assembly.
Ball-state Device — tracks ongoing ball location/count/presence as persistent state, e.g., scoop, ball lock, or trough
Players select game preferences before starting a game. Setup parameters include standard parameters applicable to all scenarios + scenario-specific parameters

blocks.title: System-Level Requirements
rows: Playing field ball action and control will be similar to a traditional, full sized pinball machine (1 1/16" dia balls, 40" x 20.5" playing field, 6.5-7 deg slope). Audio, graphics, and video are used to enhance the gaming experience including real-time game scenario progress
System supports user selectable game scenarios. Scenarios have unique themes that use the same generic playing field
Game parameters will be selected by the player before each game is started. Example parameters include: game difficulty level, number of players, player names, scenario, scenario specific parameters
Master power ON, monitor presents setup prompts which player selects
Player uses onscreen game info to identify best scoring targets
Player launches ball onto playing field using shooter
Player uses flippers and programmable buttons (DP-20 Programmable button) to keep ball in play and interact with the game to maximize score
Repeat steps G-02–G-04 until turn is over
Portable system, played on tabletop, stored in typical household closet

Use COTS parts and materials including modern electronics to replace traditional electro-mechanical, analog devices. Fab and assembly using standard workshop equipment plus 3D printer and 40W laser (24"x12" bed)
Electrical design will comply with industry-standard safety practices

blocks.title: Power Design
rows: Fused mains input; DP-13 master power switch — mains-rated toggle, accessible, visible shutoff. Fuse rating TBD (pending supply AC rating)

24V DC supply, current rating TBD, to all solenoid positive terminals through fused feeds F1–F7 and to the 24V inductive proximity sensors through fused feed F8 (Table 5.3-4). Topedal board provides low-side drivers only (no positive supply, filter, or fuse on board)
Capacitor bank across the 24V rail at the distribution point. Value TBD
Bleeder resistor across the bank; LED driven from capacitor voltage (on = charged); posted wait-time label. Discharge time TBD
Slow-blow fuse per feed F1–F8 (Table 5.3-4), rated above hold/operating current and below sustained-fault level. Ratings TBD

Separate fused 5V DC supply, regulated at 5.0V (WS2812B maximum 5.3V), to Topedal J4/J5 and J6 (level shifter, Neopixel strip) and the Hall sensor boards (DC-05/06/07). No series diodes on the rail. Rating TBD
Blue Pill powered over its USB link to the host; board 3.3V from the Blue Pill regulator

GND (coil supply return) and GNDREF (3V3/5V return) are separate nets on the Topedal board; tied at one point externally, at the GND bar (Table 5.3-4); tie verified before coil power is applied. GND bar location TBD
Each Topedal board has a unique, verified chain address before coil power is connected
Solenoid feed and return wire 18 AWG (Table 5.3-4). Supply-to-bus-bar trunk and F8 sensor feed gauge TBD. Connectors TBD

blocks.title: Rev 1.1; verified against the V02 Gerber nets and the board photos. Data is carried on the drawing; this table is the net-by-net list of the same data.

rows: Topedal Rev 1.1 schematic (Figure 5.3-2) and Blue Pill data (Figure 5.3-3); LQFP48 pins, timers and 5 V tolerance from ST DS5319 Rev 20 Table 5. Pin-to-GPIO mapping is the symbol pin order against the verified header order
Direct inputs are Sw1–Sw7 and, by repurposing the matrix header, C0–C7 and R0–R7. Sw7 (PB5), C1–C7 (PC13–PC15, PA0–PA3) and R0–R5 (PA4–PA7, PB0, PB1) are 3.3 V only and are not 5 V tolerant
Drv8 (PA13) and C0 (PA14) are the SWD pins; Sw4–Sw6 (PA15, PB3, PB4) are JTAG pins at reset; Drv5 and Drv6 (PA10, PA9) are USART1 pins. OPP firmware behaviour on these pins is not verified
Only Drv1–Drv7 have a timer output; Drv8 (PA13) has none
